item.title: Furthermore, wanderers, the brahmin says thus: 'I am not anyone's, not anything's anywhere, nor am I anything anywhere. There is nothing belonging to me anywhere,…
item.description:
Furthermore, wanderers, the brahmin says thus: 'I am not anyone's, not anything's anywhere, nor am I anything anywhere. There is nothing belonging to me anywhere, in any way.' The brahmin who says this speaks the truth, not falsehood. Therefore, he does not think of 'ascetic,' does not think of 'brahmin,' does not think 'I am superior,' does not think 'I am equal,' does not think 'I am inferior.' Furthermore, by directly knowing the truth contained therein, he practices the path of nothingness.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.185
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple reflects: 'Present sensual pleasures and future sensual pleasures, present perceptions of sensual pleasure and future perceptions of sensual pleasure, present…
item.description:
Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple reflects: 'Present sensual pleasures and future sensual pleasures, present perceptions of sensual pleasure and future perceptions of sensual pleasure, present forms and future forms, present perceptions of form and future perceptions of form, both are impermanent. What is impermanent is not fit to be delighted in, not fit to be welcomed, not fit to be clung to.' While he practices thus, abides thus often, his mind becomes calm in that element. With a calm mind, he either attains the imperturbable here and now, or he is strongly inclined towards wisdom. With the breakup of the body after death, this situation occurs: that evolving consciousness may, following this, attain the imperturbable.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 106 – Āneñjasappāyasutta

item.title: Sorrow, lamentation, and suffering, Various kinds exist in the world. They arise dependent on attachment; Without attachment, they do not arise. Therefore, those who are…
item.description:
Sorrow, lamentation, and suffering,
Various kinds exist in the world.
They arise dependent on attachment;
Without attachment, they do not arise.
Therefore, those who are happy,

Without sorrow in the world,
Are those who have no attachments.
Therefore, whoever wishes
To be without sorrow, without attachment,
Should not form attachment
To anyone in the world.

From: Udāna 8.8
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Samaṇa Gotama abstains from taking what is not given, avoids taking what is not given, takes only what is given, desires only what is given,…
item.description:
Samaṇa Gotama abstains from taking what is not given, avoids taking what is not given, takes only what is given, desires only what is given, lives purely without theft. — Bhikkhus, these are the praises of the Tathāgata by ordinary people. Samaṇa Gotama abstains from sexual misconduct, leads the holy life, lives detached, abstains from base sensual desires. Bhikkhus, these are the praises of the Tathāgata by ordinary people.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 1 – Brahmajālasutta

item.title: Brahmin, wisdom is purified by virtue, virtue is purified by wisdom. Where there is virtue, there is wisdom; where there is wisdom, there is virtue.…
item.description:
Brahmin, wisdom is purified by virtue, virtue is purified by wisdom. Where there is virtue, there is wisdom; where there is wisdom, there is virtue. One with virtue certainly has wisdom; one with wisdom certainly has virtue. Virtue and wisdom are considered supreme in the world.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 5 – Kūṭadantasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Nun Sañjā: Leaving home, going forth, I abandoned my children, Abandoned precious livestock, Abandoned greed and hatred, And regarding ignorance, I live in seclusion.…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sañjā:

Leaving home, going forth,
I abandoned my children,
Abandoned precious livestock,
Abandoned greed and hatred,
And regarding ignorance,
I live in seclusion.
Having conquered
The root of craving itself,
I live cooled,
Peaceful and calm.

From: Therīgāthā 1.18
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: ( Blessed One ) One who gives with faith, With a pure mind, Enjoys that food In this life and the next. Therefore, avoid stinginess,…
item.description:
( Blessed One )
One who gives with faith,
With a pure mind,
Enjoys that food
In this life and the next.
Therefore, avoid stinginess,
Give, remove the stain,
Beings still enjoy
Merit in the next life.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.23

item.title: Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not delight in sleeping, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.
item.description:
Bhikkhus, as long as the bhikkhus do not delight in sleeping, then the bhikkhus will prosper and not decline.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are five strands of sensual pleasure. What are the five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are five strands of sensual pleasure. What are the five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual desire, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear ... (as above) ... odors cognizable by the nose ... flavors cognizable by the tongue ... tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual desire, enticing. Bhikkhus, these are the five strands of sensual pleasure.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 26 – Ariyapariyesanāsutta

item.title: And, bhikkhus, what is a person with a mind like a wound? Here, bhikkhus, a person is irritable and very resentful; even when spoken to…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, what is a person with a mind like a wound? Here, bhikkhus, a person is irritable and very resentful; even when spoken to lightly, he becomes exasperated, angry, hostile, and displays irritation, hatred, and bitterness. Just as a festering wound, if struck by a stick or a shard, discharges even more pus, so too, bhikkhus, here a person is irritable and resentful. This, bhikkhus, is called a person who is like a festering wound.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.25
